description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between co-occurrence number and accuracy percentage (ACC) across six different methods for editing large language models in the context of long-tail biomedical knowledge. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, with tick marks at approximately $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is linear and spans from 60% to 80%, with tick labels at 5% intervals. Six distinct lines represent different methods: "Base" (black, circular markers) starts at approximately 64% ACC at a co-occurrence number of 5 and increases to about 72% at the highest co-occurrence number; "FT" (blue, downward-pointing triangles) begins at around 65% and rises to roughly 74%; "IKE" (red, upward-pointing triangles) starts at about 67% and reaches nearly 76%; "MEND" (brown, diamond markers) begins at approximately 68% and ends near 79%; "MEMIT" (purple, pentagon markers) starts at about 70% and increases to around 80%; and "ROME" (green, square markers) begins at approximately 75% and climbs steadily to about 85%. All methods show a general upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with "MEMIT" exhibiting the steepest rate of improvement. A legend in the top-left corner identifies each method by its corresponding line style and color.

Each line follows a generally upward trend as the co-occurrence number increases, with 'MEMIT' showing the steepest rate of improvement. A legend is given in the top left, describing the line and color.
